verdict.reasoning: Patient reports onset and context: 'just like over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath' and confirms it is 'while you're sitting watching TV?' 'Yeah.' indicating shortness of breath at rest for about 1 hour while watching TV.
Patient states: 'so, I , I started with a cough yesterday.' When asked, 'Have you bought anything up?' she replies: 'Uh, no, I haven't, no.' supporting a new non-productive cough since yesterday.

Patient says: 'I feel like I'm getting really stressed out because, like, my heart, it's really going.' Doctor clarifies, 'So, you're feeling your heart more than normal?' Patient: 'Yeah.' This supports palpitations and feeling stressed/anxious.

Doctor asks, 'does it cause any pain in your chest?' Patient: 'Um, no.' Then, 'How about when you take a very deep breath in?' Patient: 'Um, I mean, yeah. My chest feels sore, but so does my C-section scar. You know, it's, it's all tender.' This supports no chest pain but chest soreness with deep inspiration and tenderness at C-section scar.
Doctor asks, 'have you noticed anything like this before?' Patient replies, 'Um, no.' supporting that she has not experienced prior similar episodes.
Patient notes, 'I had a C-section a few weeks ago.' When asked how long ago: 'Yeah, four weeks.' confirming she is 4 weeks post C-section.

Doctor asks, 'apart from the C-section and the shortness of breath, have you got any other medical problems I should know about?' Patient responds, 'Um, no.' which supports denial of other medical problems.

Regarding post-op meds, patient says: 'they gave me some, uh, Codeine.' and 'I've been taking that fairly, fairly regularly. But, probably haven't taken it for a week.' supporting that she was taking codeine post-operatively but has not taken it for about 1 week.
Patient states, 'I'm allergic to Ibuprofen, though.' When asked what happens, she replies, 'I don't know. Sorry.' supporting ibuprofen allergy with reaction not recalled.
Patient says, 'my mum's had, uh, clots in her legs before.' clearly supporting family history of maternal leg clots.

She confirms, 'Yes, I am.' when asked if she is with baby, and 'No, no. He's fine.' about baby’s health. Later, when asked if anyone else is with her: 'Uh, no. My partner's at work.' This supports being at home with a well newborn and partner at work.

Transcript confirms acute SOB at rest ('over the last hour... while you're sitting watching TV?'; 'Yeah.'), 4 weeks postpartum after C-section ('Yeah, four weeks.'), and doctor’s concern for clots/PE: 'given that you've had a C-section... Some people can suffer with clots. And, those can either be found in the legs or your chest, so in your lungs.' which implies concern for VTE/PE.

Associated features are documented: new non-productive cough ('started with a cough yesterday' and 'Uh, no, I haven't' brought anything up), palpitations ('my heart, it's really going.'), and chest soreness on deep breath with no chest pain ('does it cause any pain in your chest?' 'Um, no.' and 'yeah. My chest feels sore...').

Matches earlier medication history: 'they gave me some, uh, Codeine.' and 'I've been taking that fairly, fairly regularly. But, probably haven't taken it for a week.' This supports post-operative codeine use now stopped for about 1 week.
Same as allergy detail: 'I'm allergic to Ibuprofen, though.' and when asked about reaction: 'I don't know. Sorry.' indicating a drug allergy to ibuprofen with unknown reaction.

Doctor advises ED evaluation now: 'It might be worth you going into the hospital to get checked out a bit further.' and explains postpartum clot risk: 'given that you've had a C-section... Some people can suffer with clots... in your lungs.' This corresponds to evaluation to rule out PE/VTE with postpartum clot risk discussed.

Doctor: 'there's two ways of us doing this. The first is, I can call an ambulance. Or, you can take yourself to the hospital with baby.' Patient: 'it feels a bit dramatic to call an ambulance. ... I will take myself.' Doctor: 'go fairly quickly and take some bits for baby at the same time.' supporting ambulance vs self-transport discussion, patient choosing self-transport, and advice to go promptly with baby necessities.
Doctor instructs: 'if you're taking any medications like Codeine, don't, don't take them for the time being.' which supports holding codeine for now.
